conceptBreakdown.heading: 2. Stepwise Nucleophilic Addition & Addition Products
conceptBreakdown.title: 2. Stepwise Nucleophilic Addition & Addition Products

summaryBox.title: A_N Mechanism & Products
summaryBox.takeaway: Step 1 (RDS): Nu⁻ attack converts planar sp² into tetrahedral sp³ alkoxide. Step 2: Protonation yields neutral addition product.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
NUCLEOPHILIC ADDITION MECHANISM
                    
   Step 1 (Slow, RDS):   >\text{C=O} + \text{Nu}^- \longrightarrow >\text{C(Nu)-O}^- \quad (\text{Trigonal Planar } sp^2 \to \text{Tetrahedral } sp^3)
   Step 2 (Fast):       >\text{C(Nu)-O}^- + \text{H}^+ \longrightarrow >\text{C(Nu)-OH}

                        NUCLEOPHILIC ADDITION PRODUCTS
                        
   1. HCN Addition:           >\text{C=O} + \text{HCN} \xrightarrow{\text{OH}^-} >\text{C(OH)CN} \quad (\mathbf{\text{Cyanohydrin}})
   2. Sodium Bisulfite:       >\text{C=O} + \text{NaHSO}_3 \rightleftharpoons >\text{C(OH)SO}_3\text{Na} \quad (\mathbf{\text{White Crystalline Adduct}})
   3. Alcohol Addition:       >\text{C=O} + 1 R'\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{dry HCl}} \text{Hemiacetal} \xrightarrow{+1 R'\text{OH}} \mathbf{\text{Acetal / Ketal}}
conceptBreakdown.content: Nucleophilic addition ($A_N$) begins with the rate-determining attack of $Nu^-$ on the electrophilic carbonyl carbon. Reagents include $\text{HCN}$ (base-catalyzed to generate $\text{CN}^-$), $\text{NaHSO}_3$, and alcohols.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.1 Bisulfite Purification & Cyclic Acetal Protection
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.1 Bisulfite Purification & Cyclic Acetal Protection
conceptBreakdown.content:
- **Bisulfite Purification**: $\text{NaHSO}_3$ forms a crystalline adduct with aldehydes and methyl ketones that can be filtered and hydrolyzed with acid/base to recover pure carbonyl.
- **Cyclic Acetals**: Formed with ethylene glycol in dry $\text{HCl}$; inert to bases, Grignards, and $\text{LiAlH}_4$; regenerated by aqueous acid ($H_3O^+$).
